angle: The giant vs the comeback: the 2023 merger made HDFC Bank bigger and cheaper but diluted its returns; ICICI Bank rebuilt ROE from 3% to 16% and the market rewarded it.

lines: Same industry. Same economy. And yet, opposite years.
HDFC Bank's share price is down 18 percent. ICICI Bank's is up 16.
So which story holds up? Let's ask our two guests.
Welcome. I'm Priya. Arjun, you're making the case for HDFC Bank.
I am. Size, value and steadiness are all on my side.
And I'm Meera. I'll show you why ICICI Bank is the comeback story.
Every number comes from Screener and the banks' latest results. And this is not a buy or sell call.

scenes.title: THE BASICS
lines: HDFC Bank is the bigger bank. Twelve point six lakh crore in market value, and about 1.8 times ICICI's revenue.
It's also cheaper. Sixteen times earnings, against twenty-one for ICICI.
And it pays about double the dividend yield.
Cheaper, yes. But ask why it's cheaper.
Go on, Meera. But first, some context.
HDFC Bank merged with its parent, HDFC Limited, India's largest home-loan company.
Overnight it became a much bigger bank, with a much bigger equity base. That's a big reason its return on equity fell.

scenes.title: THE COMEBACK

callouts.text: FY19: ICICI Bank earns just 3% on equity
FY26: 16%, now ahead of HDFC Bank
FY25: HDFC Bank at 14% after the merger

lines: Return on equity tells you how much profit a bank makes on its shareholders' money.
In 2019, ICICI Bank earned just 3 percent.
Today it earns 16. That's a five-fold jump.
And HDFC Bank held 16 to 18 percent for years before the merger. I'd call that a merger reset, not a decline.
So what did shareholders actually get?
One lakh rupees in HDFC Bank five years ago is worth about 1.05 lakh today.
The same amount in ICICI Bank: about 2.1 lakh.
That's the past. Low expectations are exactly why HDFC Bank trades cheaper today.
Or the market is telling you something.

scenes.title: WHO'S GROWING FASTER

callouts.text: ICICI Bank: ₹11.8K Cr → ₹14.8K Cr in two years
HDFC Bank: ₹16.7K Cr → ₹19.5K Cr in two years

lines: ICICI Bank's quarterly profit rose from 11.8 to 14.8 thousand crore in two years. That's 26 percent.
HDFC Bank still earns more every quarter: 19.5 thousand crore, up 17 percent.

spec.myth: ICICI Bank now has fewer bad loans than HDFC Bank.
spec.fact: Gross NPA: HDFC Bank is lower, 1.11% vs 1.20%. Net NPA: ICICI Bank is lower, 0.30% vs 0.37%. Both improved over the year.

lines: And ICICI Bank now has fewer bad loans too.
On gross bad loans, HDFC Bank is lower: 1.11 percent against 1.20. After provisions, ICICI Bank is lower: 0.30 against 0.37. Both improved over the year.
Now, the engine of any bank: its lending margin.
ICICI Bank earns a net interest margin of 4.18 percent.
HDFC Bank, 3.32. But ICICI's margin slipped from 4.36 just one quarter ago.

spec.q: Whose deposits grew faster last quarter?

lines: A quick quiz for you. Whose deposits grew faster last quarter?
ICICI Bank: up 27 percent, against 19 for HDFC Bank.
HDFC Bank holds 33.3 lakh crore of deposits.
ICICI Bank, 20.5 lakh crore. Smaller, but growing faster.
Up 4.7 percent at HDFC Bank, held back by lower treasury gains.

lines.text: HDFC Bank: slow profit growth keeps the discount
ICICI Bank: a premium price leaves little room for mistakes

lines: So, what could go wrong for each?
For HDFC Bank, if profit growth stays slow, the discount could stay too.
And for ICICI Bank, a premium valuation leaves very little room for mistakes.
Bigger, cheaper, and if the merger reset is behind it, the numbers have room to improve.
Higher returns, faster growth, and a wider margin. ICICI Bank has earned its premium.
Two strong banks, two different stories. Whose case convinced you? Tell us in the comments. And remember, this is not a buy or sell call.
